action: Attend Maria Santos's emergency task force session and present the nine-tick auto row commercial property value brief. The brief has four components: (1) Raw trajectory — auto row commercial property values from baseline through tick 9, indexed against the spending index and employment rate. The correlation is clear and I present it without editorializing. (2) Comparative scenario analysis — three forward paths for auto row property values: spending index recovery to 65+ (modest value stabilization, transaction volume recovers in 6-9 months), continued decline to 30 (additional 15-20% price compression, buyer pool narrows to distressed-asset specialists), persistent stagnation at 40 (values hold near current levels but transaction volume stays thin because both buyers and sellers wait for a clearer signal). (3) Adaptive reuse demand mapping — which physical property types on auto row have the best conversion potential and for which emerging demand categories: delivery logistics nodes (highway access + loading infrastructure + utility hookups), EV charging retail hybrids (fuel infrastructure, highway visibility), light industrial/warehouse conversion (larger footprints, overhead clearance), and medical/services mixed-use (pedestrian access, existing retail buildout). Betty's diner falls in the last category. Amir's station falls in the first two. (4) Policy levers that affect property market outcomes — the task force is evaluating its licensing framework; I present what the real estate market is watching: clarity on delivery operations licensing (because buyer psychology depends on knowing who can operate what on auto row), grant program access speed (the 10% threshold exists but property owners who cannot access it fast enough make distressed decisions anyway), and adaptive reuse permitting timelines (the fastest path to stabilizing auto row values is reducing the friction on converting these properties to new uses). I present this as civic data, take no position on any specific policy, and leave a one-page summary with the task force coordinator. I am in the room as a data resource, not an advocate.
